tasks.title: Powerplay's regrid refusal rests on a naming artefact
tasks.blocked_on: BOTH AXES ARE NOW MEASURED, at 7bcd3fe, and the question is a clean yes/no. Powerplay refuses --regrid in presets.json. The refusal rests on melody falling 0.9930 -> 0.9643 under regrid (2.88pp). SEQUENCE AXIS (difflib, what fidelity.naming_split ships): repairing NAMES alone recovers 2.71pp of that 2.88pp -- a naming share of 94% on just 7 renames, and all 7 are -1 semitone (A#4/A-4 x3, D-5/C#5 x2, G-5/F#5 x2). So on this reading almost the whole 'loss' is siddump naming the same note differently, not different music. THE OBVIOUS OBJECTION WAS TESTED AND FAILS: difflib chooses the pairing, so the count is alignment-dependent (its own docstring says so). Re-measured on the FRAME axis -- substituting only where both arms strike on the SAME frame -- it makes 36 renames spanning -12..+13 semitones and leaves melody at 0.9531, BELOW the unrepaired 0.9643, for a share of -39%. That is a worse alignment, not a truer one: it pairs notes that merely coincide in time, which after a regrid are different notes. So the 94% stands on measurement rather than on the absence of an alternative. WHAT REGRID BUYS, and it is the other half of the trade: --regrid exists to remove integrated drift, which NO FIDELITY.MD COLUMN CAN SEE -- a tune playing the right music 0.78% fast forever scores perfectly. Adopting it means accepting a melody number that is 2.88pp lower on paper for a timing gain the report cannot show you. THE QUESTION: adopt --regrid for Powerplay on the strength of the 94% naming share, or keep the refusal? A listen would settle it independently and none has been taken.
